avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, action against the emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: The City buys trees and pays to have them planted on sidewalks, in parks and on private land. It also funds the machinery and employee teams who do this work in the boroughs. At the same time, borough councils allow construction projects to depart from the rules on trees and greening.

etapes.titre: Contracts for planting trees on public land
etapes.texte: City council awards two contracts to supply and plant 1,374 trees in seven boroughs, then water them, maintain them and replace some of them. The maximum expense is $2,456,590.55, taxes included.

The City is paying $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional land until December 31, 2026. Pierrefonds-Roxboro is separately transferring $162,233.12 from its parks fund to buy trees and plants.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an expansion on rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening instead of the required 40 trees and 25%. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is renting a mini backhoe loader with operator for $152,916.75 and setting aside $200,000 for blue-collar teams assigned to planting. Outremont is awarding the renovation of the parc Pratt chalet and the redevelopment of its surroundings, including planting vegetation, for an expense of $800,416.17, financed in part by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

The City is leasing plots in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for $100, so it can operate a transition nursery there. The lease runs for 24 months starting May 1, 2026, and the property subsidy is estimated at $329,600.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit a progress report on October 31, 2026, its accountability report by December 31, 2026 at the latest, then its summary and financial statements on March 31, 2027.
The 855 trees in lot 2 must be planted in spring 2027; watering, maintenance and replacement continue until the end of November 2029.
The transition nursery lease ends on April 30, 2028.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and snow loading contracts, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.

etapes.texte: Several boroughs are renting sweeper trucks, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and a mini sweeper with operators to remove abrasives from streets, sidewalks and bike paths in the spring. In Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, the sidewalk cleaning contract for four private snow removal sectors guarantees about 278 km of sidewalks per year [CA26 27 0034].

etapes.titre: Snow removal at downtown public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie is hiring companies to maintain, clean and remove snow from Square Viger, Place des Montréalaises, square Dorchester, place du Canada, îlot Bonaventure, square Victoria, place du Sable-Gris and square Chaboillez. The borough is also extending snow removal in the Quartier des Spectacles by one year, from April 2, 2026 to April 1, 2027 [CA26 24 0067].

Montréal-Nord is paying for an additional rented grader due to winter conditions, and Saint-Léonard is drawing $200,000 from its surpluses for wages and the purchase of abrasives, after 39 spreading operations since November 15, 2025 [CA26 13 0121]. Verdun is offering to supply its own staff at the snow disposal site for 2025, 2026 and 2027.

The City is extending turnkey snow removal contracts by twelve months in Anjou, Montréal-Nord and Pierrefonds-Roxboro, towing contracts in four boroughs, and equipment rentals with operator in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie. Ville-Marie and Ahuntsic-Cartierville are extending front-end loader tractor rentals.

Anjou is amending the fine amounts in its by-law on snow removal of properties by contractors, and Ahuntsic-Cartierville is amending its by-law on snow removal and clearing. Saint-Léonard is tabling a draft by-law requiring snow removal contractors working on private commercial, industrial or institutional properties to hold a permit.

aSurveiller.texte: The turnkey snow removal contracts for Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Lachine, Outremont and Sud-Ouest end on April 15, 2030, with each season running from November 1 to April 15.
The turnkey snow removal contract for Le Plateau-Mont-Royal ends on April 15, 2031.
Snow removal on service roads and parking lots at the Grand parc de l'Ouest runs from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
Snow removal and maintenance of the esplanade Tranquille is extended from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: The City is financing and building the disinfection plant at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, and is having its equipment maintained. It is also awarding contracts to rehabilitate or rebuild water and sewer pipes on many streets, and to replace lead service lines, including the portion on private property. At the same time, it is passing loan by-laws to pay for this work.

etapes.texte: The City is increasing from $197,000,000 to $381,000,000 the loan that finances the effluent disinfection unit at the Jean-R.-Marcotte plant. The money is used to finish the ozonation unit, install liquid oxygen tanks and build the oxygen production plant.

The City is awarding several contracts to rehabilitate secondary water pipes without digging trenches and to redo the roadway, on streets in the west, north, centre and east of the island. Each contract also includes replacing lead water service connections, on both the public and private sides.

aSurveiller.texte: The ozone plant at the Jean-R.-Marcotte plant is expected to come into service in 2029, and the contracts for lots 4, 5 and 6 are to be completed in the last quarter of 2028.
Work on rue de la Cathédrale, between rue Saint-Jacques and the McTavish reservoir, is to be completed in March 2027 instead of December 2026.
The construction site on rue Guy, between Saint-Jacques and René-Lévesque, is to continue until December 2027.
The shutdown of sludge incinerator 4 at the Jean-R.-Marcotte plant is planned for January 2027, for about six weeks of work.
The intrusive-method inspection of main pipes is to be completed in June 2028.

frederic-back.titre: Frédéric-Back Park and Saint-Michel Environmental Complex
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned dump, transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, and electrical upgrades.
frederic-back.enBref: This year, the City is continuing work on Frédéric-Back park, within the Saint-Michel Environmental Complex. It is launching construction of a greenhouse complex led by the borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, having the electrical installation linked to biogas capture modernized, and giving park maintenance contracts to companies. It is also requesting money from the Québec and Canada governments for a pedestrian and bike link and for the park's development.

etapes.titre: Funding request for the east-west link
etapes.texte: The City is asking the Québec ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable for funding of up to $2,000,000 for a 900-metre trail crossing the park from east to west, with a footbridge of about 150 metres. The project includes rainwater management works and a 12.7-hectare meadow.

The conseil d'agglomération approves a complex of research, training and community production greenhouses in the park's southwest sector, with a construction budget estimated at $2,185,000, and hands the project to the city council, which passes it on to the borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension. The borough then awards Les industries Harnois inc. a contract worth $499,865.92, taxes included, to supply and install two greenhouses.

The City awards Systèmes Urbains inc. the second phase of the electrical upgrade work at the Saint-Michel Environmental Complex, for a total expense of $1,255,447.38, taxes included. The work covers a new 25 kV power supply, a transformer, a backup generator and a controller that manages biogas capture.

The City awards general park maintenance to 178001 Canada inc. (Groupe Nicky) and ecological and horticultural management to 9190-8673 Québec inc. (Les Entreprises Roseneige) for 30 months. It is also extending the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor, whose compost is used for park landscaping, as well as the snow removal contract for the park, the TAZ and the soccer stadium.

The borough awards Groupe MPotvin a contract worth $8,199,514.82, taxes included, to redevelop rue De Louvain between the park and boulevard Saint-Michel: sewers, water mains, lighting, sidewalks, bike facilities and plantings. In October, it authorizes filing a funding request with the Véloce III program of the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable for the bike lane and sidewalks.

aSurveiller.texte: The call for projects under the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable's TAPU program ends on November 26, 2026.
Greenhouse installation work must be completed by December 2026, with commissioning announced for winter 2027.
Snow removal for the park, the TAZ and the soccer stadium is extended until April 30, 2027.
Park maintenance contracts run until October 31, 2028, and 26 more hectares will be added in 2027 in the Boisé Ouest sector.
The rue De Louvain construction site runs in three phases: May to November 2026, May to October 2027, then May to August 2028.

grand-parc-ouest.description: Canada's largest municipal park, in the making: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.
grand-parc-ouest.enBref: This year, the City is maintaining and protecting the sectors of the Grand parc de l'Ouest. It adjusted a contract for the repair of heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, filed a candidacy for an international designation related to the night sky at Cap-Saint-Jacques, and had two sectors listed in a registry of protected natural areas. It also awarded contracts for culvert reconstruction, snow removal, tree felling and housekeeping.

etapes.titre: More money for the heritage walls
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98, taxes included, to the contract for the repair of the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77. Buried stones, extra mortar and a degraded culvert explain the increase, according to file 1255414002.

The City files the candidacy of the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector (330 hectares) for DarkSky International's Urban Night Sky Place designation. It commits to producing a lighting plan, bringing its light fixtures up to standard, and keeping night-time access open to the public.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as natural areas
etapes.texte: The parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector (429 ha) are listed in the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité, with conservation plans. Elected officials also take note of the 2025 summary of the areas.

The City awards contracts for snow removal on the service roads and parking lots of Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche and Cap-Saint-Jacques, as well as housekeeping for nine buildings at Cap-Saint-Jacques, including the chalet d'accueil, the Maison Richer and the Château Gohier.

aSurveiller.texte: Snow removal of roads and parking lots from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028, with no possible extension.
Housekeeping of the nine buildings at Cap-Saint-Jacques from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030, with a possible extension until October 31, 2031.
Tree felling planned from fall 2026 to early summer 2028.
For the night sky designation: lighting plan filed in February 2027, response from DarkSky expected in April 2027, site compliance upgrade in April 2032.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: This year, the City is lending municipal buildings to organizations to open warming centres, funding organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness, and sharing a public works team dedicated to cleanliness related to homelessness across boroughs. It also sets rules for receiving private donations for shelter and housing projects, and awards contracts for support services toward housing.

etapes.texte: The City is lending three buildings free of charge to organizations for the winter: the church at 5600, 12e Avenue to Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal, the former monastery of the Recluses Missionnaires at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est to Projets Autochtones du Québec, and the Bain St-Denis at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN. Ahuntsic-Cartierville confirms the continuation of COHAB's contract for a warming centre, for a maximum amount of $126,615.07, taxes included.

Verdun pays $12,950 to Société de développement social to keep two outreach workers in its municipal facilities from January 5 to February 6, 2026. The urban agglomeration council grants $5,407,736 to 15 organizations and a further $3,942,461 to 10 already-funded organizations, for projects ending December 31, 2028.

etapes.titre: Declaration and framework for private donations
etapes.texte: City council adopts a declaration of support for people experiencing homelessness and recognition of the organization Maison Mobile. The urban agglomeration council then adopts a mechanism to govern private money donations intended for housing, shelter and social cohabitation projects. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie transfers $250,000 for the development work on the Bain Saint-Denis warming centre.

etapes.titre: Encampments, support services and legal appeal
etapes.texte: The City awards a sole-source contract of $149,520, taxes included, to Mission Old Brewery to help people from the rue Notre-Dame encampment area move toward shelter and housing, from July 13 to October 18, 2026. It also grants $90,000 to Réseau d'aide aux personnes seules et itinérantes de Montréal for the 2026, 2027 and 2028 editions of the Nuit des sans-abri. The executive committee authorizes an appeal of the June 8, 2026 ruling on the encampments under the Van Horne viaduct.

etapes.titre: Extended shuttle services and encampment program
etapes.texte: The City extends until December 31, 2027 the shuttle service agreements with Projets Autochtones du Québec, Mission Old Brewery and L'Amour en action Syl Dan, with additional support of $860,692. It awards seven service contracts, for $3,025,000 taxes included, for the Programme d'interventions spécialisées en campement. Ville-Marie regulates noise for the Nuit des sans-abri on October 16, 2026, on rue Beaudry.

aSurveiller.texte: The shuttle service agreements with Projets Autochtones du Québec, Mission Old Brewery and L'Amour en action Syl Dan are extended until December 31, 2027.
Financial support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs covers a three-year period ending December 31, 2028.
Budget transfers are authorized for the Programme d'interventions spécialisées en campement in 2027, 2028 and 2029.
The public works team is active in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles from May 15, 2026 to May 15, 2027.
According to the file on the Van Horne viaduct encampments, the ruling on the merits is expected likely in 2027.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on municipal lands in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary developments.

etapes.texte: The City is extending the lease of a lot to the Société de transport de Montréal, south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent, for parking of its officers' vehicles. It is also extending the lease of a neighbouring lot to a paid parking company, for a total rent of $45,049 before taxes [CM26 0080].
City council names the new street at the heart of the Louvain eco-district "avenue des Solidarités." The name comes from a public call for proposals held in fall 2024.

etapes.titre: Street, networks and soil to be rehabilitated
etapes.texte: The City awards a contract of $10,311,940.25 including taxes to develop a street in the eco-district with sewer, waterworks, roadwork, lighting and an underground electrical network, for a total expenditure of $15,366,336 [CG26 0368]. The contract includes rehabilitation of the soil at the former gas station on the Louvain Est site, funded by the environmental liability reserve.

etapes.titre: Construction rules and money for housing
etapes.texte: The borough adopts draft by-laws and resolutions allowing more height and density on the Louvain Ouest side, with a target of 200 housing units per hectare. City council adds $48,398.55 to the infrastructure work for the modular housing on the Louvain Ouest site [CM26 1049] and gives $500,000 to the Société de développement Écoquartier Louvain to design a non-market housing project.

aSurveiller.texte: Second phase of the rue de Louvain construction site (sidewalks, curbs, bulges), from May to October 2027, then third phase (final roadway, bike path, plantings) from May to August 2028.
The loan of the lot for the vegetable garden ends on December 31, 2027.
The loan of the lot for the sunflowers and greenhouse runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027.
The parking lease with the Société de transport de Montréal begins on October 1, 2026, for three years.
Four other public spaces on the site remain to be named before the development is completed, expected around 2032.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collection, sorting centres, biomethanization and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: This year, the City is adjusting its collection rules in several boroughs, buying bins and extending contracts for processing food waste and for transport to ecocentres. It is also awarding hydro-excavation contracts with waste treatment in several boroughs. The 2025 waste management report and inspector general reports on collection subcontracting are being tabled at councils.

etapes.titre: New collection rules in the boroughs
etapes.texte: The executive committee is changing collection days, schedules and sectors in L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, where garbage is collected every two weeks from November 1 to April 30 and every week from May 1 to October 31. Two boroughs are also authorizing waste-related fittings in buildings: a storage room of at least 28 m² at 397, boulevard Saint-Joseph Ouest, and an exemption from an outdoor drop-off area at 2380, rue Notre-Dame Ouest.

The City is extending its contracts with Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. twice, by six months each time, to compost or biomethanize food waste from the eastern part of the agglomeration, at $3,269,055.43 taxes included per extension. It explains that the start-up of the Montréal-Est organic matter treatment centre is not confirmed and that it can end the contracts with 30 days' notice.

The City is entering into framework agreements to supply collection bins, including one with Plasti-Bac inc. for garbage bins intended for Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, where garbage collection will be spaced out. Ahuntsic-Cartierville is giving Ville en vert a mandate for information and awareness-raising, and the executive committee is approving an agreement with Tricentris to lend reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations for neighbourhood events.

The City is extending the contract for supplying and transporting containers for the Saint-Laurent ecocentre, as well as the contracts for collecting garbage from front-loading and semi-underground containers. It is awarding Recyc-Matelas inc. a contract worth $734,690.25 taxes included, over 28 months, to collect and recover mattresses and box springs left at ecocentres.

aSurveiller.texte: The extension of the food waste processing contracts runs until February 28, 2027.
The Saint-Laurent ecocentre container contract and the container collection contracts are extended until October 31, 2027.
The contract for the discharge authorization management software covers the period from October 12, 2026 to October 11, 2029.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former hippodrome Blue Bonnets: sale of land, loan by-laws, water main for the Namur–De la Savane sector.
namur-hippodrome.enBref: The City is preparing the ground, literally and legally, for the future neighbourhood on the site of the former hippodrome. It got more time from Quebec to sell a first piece of land, adopted loan by-laws for the water main and public works, and transferred a piece of land to an organization for non-market housing. At the same time, it is leasing parcels of the site to organizations for urban agriculture and a nursery.

etapes.titre: More time to sell a first piece of land
etapes.texte: The Government of Quebec grants the City a deadline until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The postponement does not involve any financial compensation, and the other conditions of the 2017 transfer remain the same.

The City guarantees a loan of $2,000,000 from the Canada Infrastructure Bank to Société GALOPH, a non-profit organization, to pay for feasibility studies of the residential project. The same month, city council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and management of public assets in the neighbourhood.

The City borrows $29,000,000 to develop the public domain of the neighbourhood: soil remediation, sewers and water main, street redevelopment and land purchases. It also borrows $12,000,000 to build water mains between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.

etapes.titre: Four buildings authorized on rue Namur
etapes.texte: The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a draft resolution authorizing the construction of four buildings, in four phases, at 7301 boulevard Décarie and 5150-5160 rue Namur. One of the buildings must house a municipal sports and recreation centre, and the developer will pay $3,200,000 for public works in the sector.

The City leases parcels of the site to the community cafeteria MultiCaf and to Coopérative de solidarité Polliflora for temporary urban agriculture, and to Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for a transition nursery. Each lease provides for rent of $100 or $200 before taxes, with the organizations paying for development, maintenance and property taxes.

aSurveiller.texte: The City has until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site, under the amended agreement with the Government of Quebec.
The federal grant of $128.3M is conditional on the infrastructure being completed by 2031.
MultiCaf's lease for urban agriculture ends on April 30, 2027.
The transition nursery's lease ends on April 30, 2028, and Coopérative Polliflora's lease ends on March 31, 2028.

parcs.description: Development and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: This year, the City is funding the design and redevelopment work of parks in several boroughs, from parc Le Prévost to parc Baldwin. It is also awarding maintenance and work contracts in the Grand parc de l'Ouest, and submitting the application of the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector for an international dark-sky designation. Several decisions adjust contracts already underway on park construction sites.

etapes.texte: The City awards the winning team of an architecture competition the design of the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and the redevelopment of parc Le Prévost, for a total expense of $10,559,257.81, taxes included. It also pays $174,471.56, net of taxes, to the borough of Verdun for soil and environmental studies of the parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard, built on a former dump.

The City adds $162,897.98 to the contract for the repair of the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, has a culvert under the same road rebuilt, and awards contracts for snow clearing of service roads and for cutting down ash trees and declining trees. It submits the application of the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector for the Urban Night Sky Place designation and lists the Anse-à-l'Orme sector, along with the parc-nature des Sources, in the registry of protected natural environments.

Several decisions add money or shift budgets in projects already launched: oversight of work at the parc du Bassin-à-Bois, parc des Hirondelles, parc du Sault-au-Récollet, parc Villeray, parc Percy-Walters and the museography of the parc des Sœurs de Sainte-Anne.

City council removes a former street portion of 810.2 m² from the public domain as a street in order to add it to parc Campbell Ouest. It does the same with a 75.2 m² strip of lane that runs through parc Le Prévost.

aSurveiller.texte: End of work at parc Denise-Morelle in November 2026, according to the file from the borough of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal.
Snow clearing of the Grand parc de l'Ouest from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
Housekeeping of nine buildings in the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030, with a possible extension to October 31, 2031.
For the Cap-Saint-Jacques application: lighting plan submitted in February 2027, response from DarkSky expected in April 2027, site compliance work in April 2032.
Final acceptance of work at parc du Bassin-à-Bois expected in June 2027.
End of work at parc J.O.R.-Leduc in June 2028; tree cutting in the Grand parc de l'Ouest until early summer 2028; installation of the artwork at parc des Eaux-Cachées in 2028.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and business animation by-laws.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City is organizing the 2026 season of pedestrian streets and public squares: it adopts funding rules, pays out money to boroughs and business development corporations, then closes street sections to cars and regulates sales, noise and traffic on these streets. It also settles a dispute related to the development of a public square, changes the status of a piece of land and gives a name to a square.

etapes.titre: Funding rules and settlement of a dispute
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law that allows it to subsidize its business development corporations to pedestrianize streets, up to $425 per linear metre of pedestrianized street. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to the construction work on a public square at the corner of rue Beaubien Est and rue Boyer.

The boroughs close sections to cars and authorize terraces, the sale of food and drinks, music and ground painting: Ville-Marie for thirteen streets, Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce for the Placette CDN and avenues Royal and Madison, Outremont for avenue Bernard, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve for rue Ontario Est, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal for avenues du Mont-Royal and Duluth.

The executive committee grants $40,000 to animate the pedestrian street Notre-Dame Ouest from July 10 to 19, 2026, during the FIFA World Cup. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce closes avenue de Monkland for a business promotion from August 20 to 23, 2026, and Ville-Marie authorizes a musical sound ambiance on the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles.

etapes.titre: Public squares and end of season
etapes.texte: City council names "place Chez-Marguerite" the public square at the corner of rue Charleroi and avenue L'Archevêque, in Montréal-Nord, and changes the status of an 899-square-metre piece of land from street to local park near the Langelier metro station. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal revises the reopening schedule for avenue du Mont-Royal in three sections.

aSurveiller.texte: Avenue du Mont-Royal reopens to traffic between Saint-Denis and Resther on September 30, 2026, and between Saint-Laurent and Saint-Denis on October 15, 2026.
Traffic resumes on the chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges ramp on November 1, 2026, after dismantling on November 1 and 2.
The by-law on the sound ambiance of the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles runs until September 2, 2027.
The on-demand transportation contract for avenue du Mont-Royal covers the period until December 31, 2027; the 2027 edition takes place only if the pedestrianization project is renewed.
Funding assistance for the pedestrianization of avenue Lacombe continues until December 31, 2028: $22,500 in 2027 and $20,000 in 2028.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws that each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.titre: Requests for extension to the ministère
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville is requesting twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is requesting an additional six months, after a first extension obtained in July 2025.

Following the public consultation on March 25, 2026, Ville-Marie is revising its rules on urban planning, special projects, demolition, certificates and cadastral operations. The by-law authorizes a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and allows public transit stations in category E.1 sectors.

The borough is changing the heights, uses and site coverage ratio in the sector bordered by avenue Papineau, avenue Émile-Journault, avenue André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est, and is increasing the allowable heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse. It is also amending its by-law on building demolition, following a public meeting held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: Saint-Laurent public consultation on its three draft by-laws, on October 20, 2026 at 7 p.m.
Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce: public consultation on October 21, 2026 and adoption on November 2, 2026; the deadline granted by the minister runs until December 16, 2026.
Saint-Léonard must adopt all its concordance by-laws by June 16, 2027, the date set by the minister of Municipal Affairs.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville is requesting an extension until June 16, 2027.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027 to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.
L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève plans to present its project to elected officials starting mid-June 2026 and hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

securite-publique.description: The City of Montréal's Police Department (SPVM): contracts, neighbourhood stations, council motions.
securite-publique.enBref: This year, the City mainly funded the operations of the Service de police de la Ville de Montréal (SPVM): a loan for equipment, purchases of vehicles and ammunition, maintenance and IT services contracts. It also renewed several leases for neighbourhood stations and department buildings, accepted government grants, and lent police officers to the RCMP and the Sûreté du Québec. Borough councils and city council adopted motions about the SPVM.

etapes.texte: The City accepted a $2,436,490 grant from the ministère de la Sécurité intérieure for the Section spécialisée en violence conjugale, keeping seven police positions and one civilian position. It extended the ACCES Tabac, ACCES Alcool, ACCES Cannabis and ACCEF committees, funded by the same ministry, until March 31, 2027, and received $8,000 from the Fonds d'aide aux victimes for a public information campaign on sexual assault.

The City purchased a port patrol boat with its trailer and two pickup trucks for the mounted unit, and awarded a group of firms the plans, specifications and work supervision for the permanent 9-1-1 relief centre. In October, it awarded a contract for video court appearances and video visitation rooms for the municipal court and the SPVM, and extended maintenance of the SIGAL software as well as maintenance of garage doors at its buildings.

aSurveiller.texte: The lease for the metro unit of neighbourhood station 50, at 888 boulevard De Maisonneuve Est, begins on February 1, 2027 and runs until January 31, 2037.
The patrol boat and its trailer must be delivered no later than March 1, 2027.
The ACCES Tabac, ACCES Alcool, ACCES Cannabis and ACCEF committees are extended until March 31, 2027.
Work to replace the oil heating system at the mounted unit building must be completed by September 30, 2027.
Maintenance of the SIGAL software is renewed from January 1 to December 31, 2027.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides about the network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.
transport-collectif.enBref: This year, the City approves the budget and borrowings of the Société de transport de Montréal (STM), and sells, leases or lends it land for its stations, ventilation buildings and staff. It also oversees metro construction sites and bus stops on its territory, and entrusts the STM with municipal work related to the extension of the blue line. Borough councils and city council adopt motions on the development of the network.

etapes.titre: Bus stops and construction sites overseen
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville sets up and removes bus waiting areas as part of the network redesign, and Saint-Laurent offers to take charge of building sidewalks at the new stops. Ville-Marie authorizes the STM to drill and redo the vault of the green line tunnel 24 hours a day from June 10 to July 31, 2026; the City signs an agreement to build a pavilion attached to the Wiseman ventilation building in Outremont, adds an incidental budget to the Berri-UQAM station construction site, and does not oppose the reconstruction of a bridge-tunnel over the REM.

The City entrusts the STM with carrying out its own work at the future Pie-IX and Viau stations, on rue Jean-Talon Est, and authorizes an expenditure of $3,808,451.29, taxes included. It then concludes 72-month framework agreements with Artelia Canada inc. and Stantec Experts-conseils ltée for the design, technical assistance and management of impacts from the redevelopment of the blue line corridor.

The agglomeration approves STM borrowings and amends its capital works program: analysis of replacing the MR-73 cars, extending their service life, bus priority measures, Réno-Infrastructures phase 4, repair of surface buildings, and management of technological and security risks.

City council asks Québec to study the conditions for keeping in Montréal the tunnel boring machine used for the blue line. Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles and LaSalle call for structuring public transit projects in the East and in the Grand Sud-Ouest, while Anjou asks the STM to stop the study of a reserved lane on rue Beaubien and avenue du Val-d'Anjou.

aSurveiller.texte: Approval from the Ministère des Affaires municipales expected in November 2026 for borrowings related to the MR-73 cars and the repair of surface buildings.
Work on the Rielle ventilation building, in Verdun, is to continue until December 2027.
Rue Wilderton will be closed for a maximum of two weeks during the summer 2027 vacation period, for the reconstruction of the bridge-tunnel; the work is scheduled to continue until March 2028.
The opening of the five new blue line stations is scheduled for 2031.

velo.titre: Cycling: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and bike lanes, and the bike-sharing system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City and boroughs are building and repairing bike lanes, managing car traffic around them, and buying equipment for the BIXI system. Work affects the REV Lajeunesse, rue Saint-Jacques, avenue Christophe-Colomb, and corridors in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve. The City is also settling its rents with Hydro-Québec for land used as bike paths and is asking Québec for financial help for four new projects.

etapes.texte: Outremont authorizes spending of $100,000, taxes included, for de-icing salt and abrasives spread notably on bike paths. Ahuntsic-Cartierville is renting a mini sweeper with an operator for spring cleaning of paths less than 1.8 metres wide.

Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie imposes mandatory manoeuvres on drivers on avenue Christophe-Colomb and formalizes bike lanes between rue des Carrières and rue de Bellechasse. Outremont introduces a draft by-law to turn a shared lane on avenue Lajoie into a one-way bike path, and Ville-Marie makes rue Saint-Jacques one-way eastbound between Peel and Robert-Bourassa for a section of the REV.

The City awards PBSC Solutions Urbaines inc. a sole-source contract of $4,815,802.61, taxes included, for bikes, stations and docking points compatible with BIXI, then a contract of $394,851.17, taxes included, to Laser AMP for the steel bases of the stations. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal and the Sud-Ouest each include the installation of a BIXI station in street and laneway projects.

City council approves an agreement of $125,167.62, taxes included, for unpaid rent from 2014 to 2025 on Hydro-Québec land used for bike paths, parks and gardens. It then approves a 10-year lease, starting January 1, 2026, for a strip of about 366 square metres used as a bike path in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles.

etapes.titre: Requests for financial help from Québec
etapes.texte: The City authorizes the filing of four financial assistance requests to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable to build bike lanes and sidewalks on rue de Champlain, rue Saint-Jacques, rue Guy and rue Laurier. It commits to paying at least half of the eligible expenses.

aSurveiller.texte: The new traffic directions and lane assignments on rue Saint-Jacques, related to the REV, take effect on November 6, 2026.
The lease for the bike path leased from Hydro-Québec in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles runs until December 31, 2035.
